2: ## [5.5.1] - 2026-11-13
3: ### Changed
4: - Updated the `com.unity.services.core` dependency to 1.19.0, which fixes "Attempted to get location for assembly Unity.Services.Core.Editor ... while it is unloading" being logged on every domain reload under CoreCLR.
5: - Authoring - Deploying a routing config (`.iaprouting`) now reads the routing on the server first and names the tags that the deploy removes because the file doesn't have them, also on a dry run. A failed read now fails the deploy instead of overwriting routing that was never read. The `enforceProviderTagValidation` field is no longer sent, as the server never used it; files that still have it load as before.
6: - Samples - Updated the samples to use `PurchasingController` instead of `StoreController` and the individual store, product and purchase services.
7: 
8: ### Fixed
9: - Authoring - Fixed a `403 Forbidden` error logged on every domain reload since 5.5.0 when ProjectSettings has a cloud project ID that isn't linked, or that the signed-in user can't access. Comparing catalog items against their remote counterpart is now skipped when the project isn't linked or has no catalog items. If the project's environments can't be loaded, the reason now shows as the items' status in the Deployment window instead of as a Console error.
10: - Authoring - A pending wait for the project to be linked to a cloud project no longer keeps the catalog deployment objects alive across a code reload, which leaked under CoreCLR.
11: - Google Play - `UpgradeDowngradeSubscription(Product, Product, GooglePlayReplacementMode)` no longer fails with "Sequence contains no matching element" when the old subscription isn't among the fetched purchases. It now falls back to the old product's transaction id.
12: - Insights - Purchase and session events now include the Firebase session ID when one is available and allowed. It was collected when consented to, but left out of the event sent to Unity, so it never reached Unity's purchase data.
13: - Remote catalog - Products could be missing from the remote catalog and from Payment Provider products when the environment holds more than 100 configs, because fetching stopped at the first page with fewer than 100 items. Fetching now continues until the server reports no more items.

88: ## [5.4.3] - 2026-09-03
89: ### Added
90: - Authoring - Payment Provider Routing files (`.iaprouting`) can now be created and deployed from the Unity Editor Deployment Window.
91: - Authoring - Added validation preventing deployment of catalog items whose store-specific product ID overrides conflict across different SKUs. Per-item validation also catches empty override values and duplicate store entries.
92: - Google Analytics identifiers are collected when Google Analytics is linked, or when Developer Data Collection is set to Recommended, in addition to the existing end-user ads consent requirement. Configure this in the Unity Dashboard, under Project Settings > Developer Data.
93: - GooglePlay - Added `IGoogleOrderInfo.OrderId` (accessible via `Order.Info.Google.OrderId`), exposing the Google Play order id of a purchase ([`Purchase.getOrderId()`](https://developer.android.com/reference/com/android/billingclient/api/Purchase#getOrderId())).
94: - GooglePlay - Added `IGoogleOrderInfo.PurchaseToken`, exposing the Google Play purchase token under its own name. This returns the same value as `IOrderInfo.TransactionID`, which contains the purchase token on Google Play.
95: - Authoring - When catalog items (`.ucat` or `catalog.csv`) are changed, they will now be compared to their remote counterpart if it exists. 
96: 
97: ### Changed
98: - Insights - On Unity 6000.7.0a7 and newer, the package uses the Editor's built-in Insights module to report IAP telemetry. Activating the module also collects data classed as essential to its operation, including session and app lifecycle events, device and OS attributes, and identifiers that associate telemetry with a project and session. Collection is governed by Unity's [Developer Data framework](https://docs.unity.com/cloud/en-us/developer-data-framework/overview) and can be managed per project in the Diagnostics section of Project Settings. On older Editor versions, the package reports through the existing gateway, unchanged.
99: - Authoring - `.ucat` catalog files now serialize store ID overrides as flat fields (`googleOverride`, `appleOverride`, `xboxStoreOverride`, `macAppStoreOverride`) instead of the `storeIdOverrides` array. Existing files with the array format are still read correctly.
100: - Remote Catalog - Runtime catalog requests now use the project-scoped Live Content domain.

50: ### Added
51: 
52: * Support for the Developer Data framework in Unity 6.2 and above
53:   * This supersedes the StartDataCollection and StopDataCollection methods, which are deprecated in Unity 6.2 and above (they are not deprecated in earlier editor versions that do not have the new EndUserConsent APIs)
54:   * In order to start and stop data collection, you must now use EndUserConsent.SetConsentState(...) to grant or deny consent for AnalyticsIntent
55:   * In order to request data deletion, you must still use the SDK's RequestDataDeletion method, but you must first explicitly deny consent using the EndUserConsent API
56:   * If consent has already been granted, data collection will start automatically during UnityServices.InitializeAsync(). Otherwise, data collection will start when consent is granted
57:   * When you start using the EndUserConsent API, the SDK will throw exceptions if you attempt to use methods from the original workflow. The two approaches cannot be mixed
